CATHAY HOTEL SHANGHAI FEB. 18, 1933
Dear ast Obs
We were "shanghaied" by cable when the Empress
of Asia arrived here. •
Will probably remain for another week or ten days and then go on to Manila,
by way of Hong Kong. I hope very much that we may arrive there before John
Holliday starts for home.
Shanghai is a most facinating place. The Bund which you have seen so
often in pictures, stretches for about ten long blocks along the river or
This street is flanked on one side by a parkway along the river
and on the other side by a row of modern office buildings, hotels and stores.
It is the center of the International Section. The government is directed by
a commission on which there are five Chinese, a like number of Englishmen,
Japanese, one American and
one Dane. The harbor is full of Chinese Junks,
battleships of the principal foreign powers,
freighters from all over the wide
world, oil tankers, and a meriad of what I call water-rickshas, small one man
propelled craft built somewhat along the lines of a gondola only not so neat
or well made.
The streets are filled with people of all nationalities. Traf-
fic runs, or rather crawls, on the wrong side of the
street to our way of think-
ing, and I find myself being on the point of steping in front of automobiles
several t imes a day.
The ricksha boys are legion. You pay about four cents,
our money, for the average ride. You have to ride almost everywhere in order
not to lose "face" which
seems to be the one thing to remember in this country.

Yesterday the East Lancastershire Regiment moved out of Shanghai bound
